what_its_for: Eculizumab-aagh is used to treat certain rare blood and kidney diseases. These include paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), a condition where your immune system destroys your red blood cells, and atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS), a condition that causes dangerous blood clots in small blood vessels and can harm your kidneys. It is also used to treat generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG), a muscle weakness disease, and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), a disease that attacks the nerves in your eyes and spinal cord. This medicine works by blocking a part of your immune system called complement that is causing the damage.
how_to_take: Eculizumab-aagh is NOT a pill. It is given directly into your vein (intravenous or IV infusion) by a nurse or doctor in a clinic or infusion center. Each infusion takes about 35 minutes to a few hours. You must never try to give this to yourself at home unless your doctor specifically instructs and trains you to do so. Before your very first dose, you MUST receive a vaccine against meningococcal bacteria at least 2 weeks before starting this medicine because this drug greatly increases your risk of serious meningococcal infection. If treatment must start sooner, you will need to take antibiotics to protect you until the vaccine takes full effect.
dosing: Your dose and how often you receive infusions depends on your condition, your weight, and your doctor's instructions. A typical schedule for adults with PNH or aHUS starts with weekly infusions for about 4 to 5 weeks, then switches to infusions every 2 weeks for long-term treatment. Dosing schedules for children are based on body weight. Your doctor will set the exact dose and schedule that is right for you. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never skip or change your infusion schedule on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss or are late for an infusion appointment, contact your doctor or infusion center right away to reschedule as soon as possible. Do not wait until your next scheduled appointment. Missing doses can cause your condition to get worse very quickly, especially if you have PNH. If you have PNH or aHUS and miss a dose, watch carefully for warning signs such as dark or cola-colored urine, little or no urine, confusion, chest pain, or sudden swelling, and seek emergency medical care immediately if these occur.
storage: Eculizumab-aagh is stored and prepared by your healthcare team or infusion pharmacy. You do not need to store this medication at home. The prepared solution should be kept refrigerated and used within a specific time frame as directed by pharmacy guidelines. If for any reason you are given a supply to take home, store it in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it. Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid contact with people who are sick, especially those with infections, because this medicine weakens a part of your immune system and makes it harder for your body to fight certain infections. Avoid skipping your meningococcal vaccine or any other vaccines your doctor recommends. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, especially if you have PNH, as stopping can cause a dangerous and potentially life-threatening flare. Avoid activities that could put you at risk for serious injury or infection without discussing them with your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room RIGHT AWAY if you have any signs of a serious meningococcal infection, which include sudden fever, severe headache, stiff neck, sensitivity to light, nausea or vomiting, or a skin rash with small red or purple spots. Also seek urgent care if you notice dark or tea-colored urine, signs of blood clots such as leg pain, swelling, or sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, confusion, decreased urination, extreme fatigue, or yellowing of your skin or eyes. Contact your doctor if you have any infusion reactions during or after your treatment, such as chills, hives, dizziness, or difficulty breathing. Always carry the safety card provided by your doctor that describes meningococcal warning signs.
when_it_works: Some patients begin to notice improvements within a few weeks of starting treatment, but it may take several months to feel the full benefit. For PNH patients, blood counts and symptoms may start to improve after the first few infusions. For aHUS, kidney function may begin to stabilize or improve within days to weeks. For myasthenia gravis and NMOSD, it may take several weeks to months to notice meaningful improvement in your symptoms. Every patient is different, so talk with your doctor about what to expect for your specific condition.
special_populations: Children: Eculizumab-aagh can be used in children for certain conditions. Doses are carefully calculated based on body weight and age. Children also require meningococcal vaccination before starting treatment. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not fully known how this medicine affects an unborn baby or whether it passes into breast milk. Your doctor will help you weigh the risks and benefits. Older adults: Older patients generally follow the same dosing schedule as other adults, but should be closely monitored for side effects. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor will monitor you closely if you have kidney or liver disease, as your condition may affect how you respond to treatment.
